text: The statue of Søren Kierkegaard is situated in the Royal Library Garden on Slotsholmen in central Copenhagen, Denmark. It was unveiled in 1918 and is based on an earlier statuette by Louis Hasselriis, which was created in 1878 and 1879. Kierkegaard is portrayed sitting on a chair, writing with a quill on a sheet of paper, with books placed next to him. The monument was enlarged by sculptors Carl Aarsleff and H.P. Petersen-Dan and cast in bronze at Lauritz Tasmussen's Bronze Foundry in 1918. Hasselriis' original plaster statuette is housed in the Danish National Gallery. The enlarged plaster copy was part of Aarsleff's private collection and later donated to Østfyns Museum, where it was previously displayed in the assembly hall of Nyborg Gymnasium and is now located outside the Søren Kierkegaard Auditorium in the University of Copenhagen's Department of Theology in Copenhagen. A second statue of Søren Kierkegaard in Copenhagen is found on the exterior of Frederik's Church and was created in 1972 by Knud Nellemose.
